stem: A coach blows a whistle and an RBT records how many seconds pass before the client starts running. Which measure is this?
rationale: Latency is the time from a cue until the response begins.

stem: A client put 7 of 10 laundry items in the right bin. What percentage was correct?
rationale: Percentage correct is 7 divided by 10, times 100, which equals 70%.

stem: A team is writing a target definition for yelling. Which version is measurable?

options.A: Gets very loud whenever she is frustrated or excited
options.B: Uses an angry tone with teachers and classmates
options.C: Is noisy in the hallway during every transition
options.D: Vocalizes loud enough to be heard 10 feet away

rationale: A measurable definition names an action that observers can detect and count without guessing at feelings.

stem: A client ignores a toy that was a top pick last month. What is the best next step?

options.B: Keep offering it every day so the client gets used to it again
options.C: Assume the client has a skill deficit
options.D: Conclude the toy is the function of problem behavior

rationale: Preferences change, so a new assessment shows which items work as reinforcers now.

stem: A note reads: 'Teacher announced clean-up; client dropped to the floor; teacher helped him up.' Which part is the antecedent?

options.A: The client dropped to the floor
options.C: The teacher helped him up afterward

rationale: The antecedent is the event that came right before the behavior.

stem: An RBT praises a client each time the client greets a classmate, and greetings become more frequent. What is the praise?

options.B: A prompt that is faded out

rationale: A stimulus that follows a behavior and makes it more likely is a positive reinforcer.

stem: How long should the pause between discrete trials usually be?

options.A: Several minutes, so the client can rest after each trial
options.B: None; trials run together with no gap at all
options.C: As long as the RBT needs to finish writing notes
options.D: Short, so the pace stays steady

rationale: Brief pauses keep the pace steady, which supports learning and keeps reinforcement frequent.

stem: A client names dogs in a picture book. Which result shows generalization?

options.A: Naming a real dog at the park untaught
options.B: Naming only the dog pictures in that one book
options.C: Refusing to look at the book
options.D: Naming pictures only after a prompt

rationale: Responding correctly with new stimuli and in a new setting, without further teaching, is generalization.

stem: Who sets the number of tokens needed to buy a backup reinforcer?

options.A: The client, depending on the day
options.B: The supervisor, in the written plan
options.C: Whoever is working in the room that day
options.D: The RBT, depending on the mood of the day

rationale: Token rules are part of the plan the supervisor writes, and the RBT follows them.

stem: An RBT retests a skill the client mastered three months ago to see whether it remains. What is this?
rationale: Checking a mastered skill after time has passed is a maintenance probe.

stem: A client rips up worksheets, the teacher takes them away, and ripping becomes more frequent. Which function is most likely?
rationale: Behavior followed by removal of the task, and then increasing, points to an escape function.

stem: Which response could replace a client's screaming to get a turn with a toy?

options.B: Screaming louder until a turn is given
options.C: Grabbing the toy from the other child
options.D: Walking away and sitting alone by the door

rationale: A replacement response should be appropriate and produce the same outcome the problem behavior did.

stem: A class stops reacting when a student burps loudly on purpose. After several weeks the burping drops. Which process is this?
rationale: Withholding the reinforcer that used to follow a behavior, so the behavior decreases, is extinction.

stem: A client trips and cuts a lip during a session. What is the first step?

options.A: Finish the current trial first and write the note later
options.B: Wait to tell anyone until next week
options.C: Check the client and follow the agency's injury steps
options.D: Send a text to a friend about it

rationale: Client safety comes first, and the agency's procedures list the steps to follow.

stem: A client's family moved to a new apartment this week. Why mention it to the supervisor?

options.A: Families must file a form with the agency each time
options.D: Moves can change routines and affect behavior

rationale: A move is a variable that can change routines and behavior, so the team should know.

stem: Which note sentence states a fact rather than an opinion?

options.A: He screamed for 20 seconds after the bell
options.B: He was being dramatic again just to get his way
options.C: She seemed sad and withdrawn for most of the morning

rationale: Objective notes record what was seen and heard, with counts or times, and leave out guesses.

stem: An RBT realizes they signed a note for a session that was cancelled. What should they do?

options.A: Leave it, since nobody noticed the mistake
options.B: Report it and correct the record
options.C: Cancel the next session to make up the time
options.D: Ask the family to sign a new form

rationale: Honesty means reporting the error so the record can be corrected.

stem: A neighbor asks an RBT how a client's therapy is going. What is the best reply?

options.A: Share a little, without using the client's name or details
options.B: Say it is going well and mention the diagnosis
options.C: Politely say you cannot discuss clients

rationale: Client information is confidential and is not shared without authorization.

stem: A client's father offers the RBT a paid weekend job at his shop. What is the best step?

options.A: Accept, because it is outside session hours and so does no harm
options.B: Ask the client what he thinks
options.C: Take the job but hide it
options.D: Discuss it with the supervisor first

rationale: Work for a client's family creates a multiple relationship, so the RBT raises it with the supervisor.

stem: A family says they do not celebrate birthdays, but the plan uses a birthday party as a reinforcer. What should the RBT do?

options.A: Tell the supervisor so a different reinforcer is used
options.B: Use the party anyway so the plan stays consistent for the child
options.C: Remove all reinforcers from the plan
options.D: Tell the child that the family's beliefs are wrong

rationale: Cultural responsiveness means respecting family practices and raising the conflict with the supervisor.
